Dogfood note — 2026-09-08

Read-only diagnose passes against excerpts from current Anth.us articles using the checked-in Anth.us editorial profile:
- Commodity receipts: who actually swapped (2026-09-05): 109 words, 0 findings.
- Inspected by Pudicus (2026-08-31): 101 words, 0 findings.

This is the expected result for approved house voice; no false-positive fixture was added. The offline corpus also passes: 2 must-pass/must-fail cases.

Holistic suggestion quality was not evaluated because this workspace has no configured OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_BASE_URL. A future dogfood run needs full source drafts plus an authorized resolver; do not infer quality from the deterministic test resolver.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Live whole-document suggestion dogfood — 2026-09-08

Source: current Anth.us article `https://anth.us/blog/commodity-receipts/` (1,075 words / 6,097 characters), checked with the portable Anth.us profile and an authorized OpenAI resolver.

Diagnosis emitted 1 redundancy finding, 2 voice-mismatch findings, and 6 missing-attribution findings. Three complete document candidates returned after fixes, each 1,055–1,058 words (98.7–99.1% similarity to source). They preserved the source voice including `ngl`, supplied factual-verification warnings for named-company metrics, and asked sensible editorial questions about title/byline and references.

Dogfood exposed and closed two defects:
- `LIM-d63e20`: a patch-sized 1,200-token response cap truncated normal article candidates.
- `LIM-9ca44b`: blanket evasion-term matching rejected legitimate source voice.

Caveat: this was a published article extracted from HTML, so title/byline/reference questions partly reflect extraction rather than editorial quality. No new precision/recall fixture was added until an editor judges the 9 diagnostic findings against the source.
